task: Read-only review of ProjectLibrary archive/restore/delete invariants, active selection/fallback, last-project protection and archived-only deletion.

conclusions: For a valid library, archive rejects the active ID before mutation; deleteArchived requires both archived and inactive. Consequently the final live project cannot be archived or deleted, and no automatic active-project fallback is needed.
Restore changes only the archive flag and preserves active identity. Archived selection, rename and duplication are rejected; archive/restore/delete of missing IDs throw before any mutation.

validated rejects empty libraries, missing/archived active identities and duplicate IDs; file loading and saving call validation. Arbitrary invalid decoded values are not accepted into persisted product state.

Deletion removes one indexed record and leaves activeID and unrelated records untouched. The store compares the complete expected snapshot under its transaction lock before atomic replacement, preventing a stale deletion from overwriting a concurrent restore.

Full-capacity recovery rechecks the complete confirmed archived record and preserves newer unrelated records; capacity that became available causes append without deletion. No concrete reachable defect was found in the reviewed source.
outcome.limits: Source review only. Existing assertions were inspected, not executed. No Linux, Apple/native, UI, or full-suite test run was performed. No repository files changed.

tests.result: Empty output; clean working tree at inspection.

tests.result: Assertions cover archive/restore identity, nonarchived and active deletion rejection, missing ID handling, preservation/reopen, capacity reclamation, and concurrent restore protection. Tests not run.
